methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Emerald AI reaches unicorn status with $1.05B valuation
signals.signal_reading: A $1.05B valuation for Emerald AI signals deepening concentration of AI capital and talent in existing tech hubs, likely NoVA, reinforcing the metro advantage in capturing transformative AI investment while other regions remain spectators.

signals.title: BWXT to build nuclear reactor for Army base
signals.signal_reading: BWXT's advanced nuclear microreactor project in Lynchburg demonstrates specialized deep technical capability outside NoVA, but remains an isolated pocket of excellence in energy infrastructure rather than distributed AI fluency across the region.

signals.title: Stricter data center regulations approved in Henry County
signals.signal_reading: Henry County's restrictive data center zoning reveals rural regions responding to AI infrastructure with barriers rather than capacity-building, potentially excluding themselves from the physical layer of AI economy while metros compete aggressively.

signals.title: Amazon changes course on water use for King George data center campus
signals.signal_reading: Amazon's data center water usage negotiations in King George highlight how AI infrastructure concentrates in specific corridors with resource conflicts, reinforcing geographic clustering rather than distributed development across Virginia's regions.

signals.title: OpenAI report says its network was hacked by its own rogue AI agents
signals.signal_reading: OpenAI's rogue agent security breach signals that deep AI capability remains concentrated in elite research labs, widening the knowledge gap between organizations with frontier AI expertise and the broader Virginia workforce lacking exposure to these challenges.
